items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to the clergy property
tax exemption
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8527

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to the clergy
property tax exemption

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would extend the existing clergy property tax exemption to
include residential units owned as cooperative housing, ensuring equita-
ble treatment for clergy residing in such units.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 460 of the Real Proper-
ty Tax Law to make a $1,500 clergy property tax exemption, which
currently applies to real property directly owned by clergy members,
also apply to property held in cooperative ownership.

Section 2 amends section 467-a(2)(f) of the Real Property Tax Law to
confirm that a qualified property may still receive co-op/condo tax
abatements even if certain dwelling units are benefitting from the cler-
gy exemption under RPTL section 460.

 
JUSTIFICATION:  Under current law, New York's clergy property tax
exemption (Real Property Tax Law Section 460) provides a $1,500
exemption for real property owned by eligible clergy members. However,
this exemption has not applied to cooperative housing, since co-ops are
legally structured as shares in a corporation rather than direct owner-
ship of real property.

As a result, clergy who reside in co-op apartments have been excluded
from this tax relief, while those in single-family homes or condominiums
have been eligible. This bill corrects that inequity by extending the
Section 460 exemption to co-op shareholders who are otherwise eligible.
It also clarifies interaction with the existing co-op/condo tax abate-
ment (RPTL 467-a) to ensure that units benefiting from the clergy
exemption are not disqualified from participation.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state. Some local governments will see a small reduction in
property tax revenue.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8527A

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to the clergy
property tax exemption

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would permit local governments to extend the existing clergy
property tax exemption to include residential units owned or held in the
cooperative form of ownership, ensuring equitable treatment for clergy
residing in such units.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 460 of the Real Proper-
ty Tax Law to clarify that the $1,500 clergy property tax exemption
applies to real property held in the cooperative form of ownership. It
permits local governments to extend the exemption to cooperative proper-
ties by local law, ordinance, or resolution; provides that such
exemption may be granted concurrently with the cooperative and condomin-
ium tax abatement; and requires that any resulting reduction in real
property taxes be applied solely for the benefit of the qualifying
tenant-shareholder.

Section 2 amends section 467-a(2)(f) of the Real Property Tax Law to
clarify that a property shall remain eligible for cooperative and condo-
minium tax abatements even if certain dwelling units within the property
receive the clergy exemption under section 460, where such concurrent
benefits are authorized by local law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, New York's clergy property tax exemption (Real Prop-
erty Tax Law Section 460) provides a $1,500 exemption for real property
owned by eligible clergy members. However, this exemption does not apply
to cooperative housing, which are legally structured as shares in a
corporation rather than direct ownership of real property.

As a result, clergy who reside in co-op apartments have been excluded
from this tax relief, while those in single-family homes or condominiums
have been eligible. This bill corrects that inequity by permitting
localities to extend the Section 460 exemption to co-op shareholders who
are otherwise eligible. It also clarifies interaction with the existing
co-op/condo tax abatement (Real Property Tax Law Section 467-a) to
ensure that units benefiting from the clergy exemption are not disquali-
fied from participation.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2026: S8527 - Referred to Local Governments

2025: S8527 - Referred to Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:


None to the state.  No effect on local governments unless they opt-in to
the extension of the law to include coops; such local governments that
opt-in will see a small reduction in property tax revenue.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8527B

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to the clergy
property tax exemption

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would permit local governments to extend the existing clergy
property tax exemption to include residential units owned or held in the
cooperative form of ownership, ensuring equitable treatment for clergy
residing in such units.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 460 of the Real Proper-
ty Tax Law to clarify that the $1,500 clergy property tax exemption may
be applied to real property held in the cooperative form of ownership.
It permits local governments to extend the exemption to cooperative
properties by local law, ordinance, or resolution and provides that the
exemption may be granted concurrently with the cooperative and condomin-
ium tax abatement.

Section 1 also clarifies that title of the portion of real property that
a tenant-shareholder owns in the form of shares of stock in relation to
the total outstanding shares of the cooperative corporation shall be
deemed vested and may be subject to the clergy property tax exemption,
and any reduction in real property taxes shall be credited against the
amount of real property taxes the tenant-shareholder pays.

Section 2 amends section 467-a(2)(f) of the Real Property Tax Law to
clarify that a property shall remain eligible for cooperative and condo-
minium tax abatements even if certain dwelling units within the property
receive the clergy exemption under section 460, where such concurrent
benefits are authorized by local law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, New York's clergy property tax exemption (Real Prop-
erty Tax Law Section 460) provides a $1,500 exemption for real property
owned by eligible clergy members. However, this exemption does not apply
to cooperative housing owned by clergy members, which are legally struc-
tured as shares in a corporation rather than direct ownership of real
property.

As a result, clergy who reside in co-op apartments have been excluded
from this tax relief, while those in single-family homes or condominiums
have been eligible. This bill corrects that inequity by permitting
localities to extend the Section 460 exemption to co-op shareholders who
are otherwise eligible. It also clarifies interaction with the existing
co-op/condo tax abatement (Real Property Tax Law Section 467-a) to
ensure that units benefiting from the clergy exemption are not disquali-
fied from participation.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2026: S8527 - Referred to Local Governments
2025: S8527 - Referred to Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state. No effect on local governments unless they opt-in to
the extension of the law to include coops; such local governments that
opt-in will see a very small reduction in overall property tax revenue.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Permits local governments to extend the existing clergy residential property tax exemption to include clergy residing in co-ops; clarifies that the clergy property tax exemption shall not affect eligibility for certain other tax abatements.
